qt: to the Commission Jorge Buxadé Villalba (ECR) Subject:

On 30 January 2024, Eurofound published a report on job quality and developments in social protection for the self-employed in the EU1. According to the report, the increase in the at-risk-of-poverty rate among the self-employed in Spain in the period 2019-2021 was the second highest in the EU. This dramatic change is in contrast to the requirement to demonstrate a 75 % reduction in income to access support measures during the COVID-19 pandemic, the highest percentage established in any of the 27 Member States for self-employed people to be eligible for social protection. In view of the above: 1.
In the Commission’s view, what is the root cause of the decline in the situation of self-employed people in Spain in the period in question?
Has it assessed any measures put in place by the Spanish Government since then to reverse this trend?
What is its view of the fact that self-employed people in Spain had to have lost three quarters of their income to be eligible for the government support scheme?

(25 June 2024) The Commission acknowledges the challenges of the self-employed in Spain, including the higher risks of poverty and social exclusion (2). The Commission is committed to enhancing access to social protection for workers and the self-employed. The Council adopted a recommendation (3) in 2019 and the Commission reported in 2023 (4) on Member States’ reforms improving access to social protection for the self-employed. However, Member States are competent to decide how to implement such policies and determine the eligibility criteria for related public support schemes. The Commission also monitors progress of the labour market, employment and the social situation, alongside relevant reforms, within the European Semester, for which it regularly consults representatives of the self-employed. In 2022, the Commission assessed that Spain had achieved ‘substantial progress’ on the 2020 Country Specific Recommendation to ‘effectively implement measures to provide liquidity to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and the self-employed’ based on the relevant Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP) measures implemented as of 2021 (5). Within the RRP, the Commission provided in February 2023 a positive preliminary assessment (6) of the reform of the social security contribution system for the self-employed. Other positive measures include the digital toolkit programme (7) and support under the European Social Fund Plus (ESF+) national and regional programmes.
